records.title: Neuro-associated SEMA3C+ tumour cells promote gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis via EBF2-FGF7-FGFR2-mediated tumour-endothelial crosstalk.
records.abstract: Recent studies have established that the nervous system is not merely a bystander in tumour progression but can actively remodel the tumour microenvironment through the neuro-tumour axis, thereby promoting tumour invasion, metastasis and survival. Semaphorin 3C (SEMA3C) has been reported to regulate tumour migration, angiogenesis and immune suppression, highlighting its potential role in tumour progression. Although the neuro-tumour axis has been identified in multiple cancer types, its role and underlying mechanisms in gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis (GCPM) remain unclear. We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) of GCPM tissues to profile tumour cell heterogeneity and identify tumour cell populations associated with neural-related signalling. Candidate tumour-microenvironmental interactions were further investigated using patient-derived organoids and co-culture models, and the identified signalling axis was validated using corresponding in vivo models. SnRNA-seq identified a distinct subpopulation of poorly differentiated tumour cells with pronounced stem-like properties and high SEMA3C expression. This subpopulation was associated with neural-related features and interacted with tumour-associated endothelial cells, thereby contributing to remodelling of the metastatic microenvironment. Furthermore, these cells enhanced tumour-endothelial communication by activating the fibroblast growth factor receptor-associated signalling pathway. The transcription factor early B-cell factor 2 (EBF2) regulates the expression of FGF7 within this subpopulation, thereby strengthening FGF7-FGFR2 signalling and promoting tumour progression. Functional validation further demonstrated that SEMA3C depletion impaired organoid growth and tumour-endothelial interactions, whereas disruption of the SEMA3C-EBF2-FGF7-FGFR2 signalling axis attenuated tumour growth and peritoneal tumour burden in vivo. Additional experimental validation supported the potential involvement of neural-related signalling in the SEMA3C-associated tumour cell state. Our findings identify a SEMA3C+ tumour cell subpopulation associated with neural-related signalling and suggest that SEMA3C promotes tumour-endothelial interactions through the EBF2-FGF7-FGFR2 signalling axis, providing a potential mechanistic link between neural regulation and microenvironmental remodelling in peritoneal metastasis of gastric cancer.

Genome-wide CRISPR screen reveals that Wnt signaling regulates lipid accumulation in APOE4 oligodendrocytes.
records.abstract: APOE4 is the strongest genetic risk factor for late-onset Alzheimer's disease, yet the cellular mechanisms linking APOE variants to disease risk remain unclear. We previously found that APOE4 expression causes lipid droplet accumulation in oligodendrocytes, reducing myelination, but the underlying mechanisms were unknown. Using a genome-wide CRISPR screen and assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (ATAC) sequencing in human-induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived oligodendrocytes, we identified decreased Wnt signaling and overactive glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK3B) as key regulators of lipid-droplet accumulation. Genetic and pharmacological inhibition of GSK3B reduced lipid droplets in APOE4 oligodendrocytes and increased myelination in three-dimensional iPSC-derived brain organoids. Pharmacological GSK3B inhibition also reduced lipid droplets and improved myelination in APOE4;PS19 tau transgenic mice. Together, these findings establish a mechanistic framework linking Wnt/GSK3B signaling to APOE4-driven disruptions in oligodendrocyte lipid metabolism and myelination, pointing to GSK3B as a potential therapeutic target for APOE4-associated Alzheimer's disease.

records.title: The expanding landscape of adult stem cell niches.
records.abstract: Adult stem cells reside within specialized niches that provide the local instructions needed to sustain regenerative fitness. Since the recognition that stem cells are not autonomous, the concept of the niche has widened from a local collection of supportive cells into a landscape of combinatorial microenvironments that stem cells help build rather than simply inhabit. Advances in molecular, genetic and deep imaging approaches and engineered organoid systems have shown these microenvironments to be far more diverse and dynamic than once appreciated. In this review, we consider how diverse cellular components build the stem cell niche across tissues, and how a growing set of non-cellular factors, from mechanical forces to metabolites, work alongside them to govern stem cell fate and regenerative capacity. We then ask how combinatorial niche interactions, spatial organization and reciprocal communication with stem cells support the diverse functions stem cells carry out across the lifespan. Understanding the niche as a dynamic and evolving system, rather than a fixed anatomical unit, promises insight into the fundamental mechanisms of developmental, regenerative, and pathologic stem cell function, with substantial implications for regenerative medicine.

records.title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine.
records.abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type-specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)-signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

records.title: Emerging frontiers for AI in single-cell genomics.
records.abstract: We are just over a decade into the single-cell revolution in biology, which has been coupled to the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in single-cell genomics. Most early single-cell RNA embedding models and subsequent "foundation models"-representational models pretrained on large single-cell datasets-did not gain wide traction among experimental biologists. However, as massive single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas efforts ramp up, there is a clear rationale for exploiting AI models to interpret new datasets in the context of vast existing data resources. Meanwhile, the advent of single-cell epigenetic/multiomic assays and Perturb-seq technologies presents new opportunities for AI modeling. Here, we review AI embedding and foundation models for scRNA-seq and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), extensive machine-learning efforts to exploit single-cell multiome in regulatory genomics, and AI strategies to learn "virtual cell" models from Perturb-seq, ending with a description of current limitations of single-cell AI models and an outlook for future advances.

records.title: Dynamic Graph Prior-Guided Latent Adaptation for Generalizable Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction.
records.abstract: Predicting transcriptional responses to drug perturbations in unseen cellular contexts is a central challenge in single-cell perturbation modeling. This challenge creates a need for models that combine flexible state transitions with structured biological prior knowledge. Existing data-driven models often struggle to generalize across unseen cell types, while many prior-based models rely on static biological graphs without explicitly conditioning prior influence on perturbation-specific target support. We propose DGP-LA, a dynamic graph-prior latent adaptation framework that refines biological priors and injects them as gated latent corrections within a cell-state-conditioned transition model. DGP-LA couples a transition backbone with perturbation-conditioned sparse graph refinement. It propagates gene-aligned target support over the refined graph and selectively injects the resulting topology-aware signal into the hidden representation. On Tahoe and NeurIPS, DGP-LA improves Pearson Delta relative to State by 8.7% and 35.8% for generalization across unseen cell types. In zero-shot drug perturbation response prediction on unseen cell types, it improves Pearson Delta relative to CRISP by 79.1% and 67.6%. The model also improves DE-gene recovery, response discrimination, and Hallmark pathway recovery, supporting adaptive latent integration of biological priors for more generalizable and biologically interpretable perturbation modeling. DGP-LA's source code and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/bieyl/DGP-LA and archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22155398. Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

records.title: Benchmarking biological knowledge-graph priors against single-cell foundation models for Perturb-seq prediction.
records.abstract: Perturb-seq prediction increasingly relies on either biological graph priors or single-cell foundation models, but their relative value is difficult to interpret when architectures, split definitions and graph sources vary simultaneously. We benchmarked STRING functional associations and Gene Ontology co-annotation against dense, self-edge-only and exact-degree-rewired supports in one fixed graph-attention backbone, with a separate 200-HVG STRING-GO-control-co-expression sensitivity. Four public Perturb-seq datasets, three nested gene-space scales and three optimisation seeds were evaluated on held-out guide conditions; GEARS, scGPT and Geneformer were evaluated on the same held-out conditions, output-gene panels and Pearson-r metric after model-specific validity checks. At 200 highly variable genes, STRING-GO improved the equal-dataset Pearson r by +0.016 (95% interval [+0.010, +0.022]) relative to dense support. Dataset effects were positive in Adamson (+0.017), Norman (+0.015), Replogle K562 (+0.017) and Replogle RPE1 (+0.014), and 122/200 guide conditions improved (0.61 [0.54,0.68]). The top-20-gene Jaccard difference was +0.009 [+0.006,+0.012]. STRING-GO exceeded self-edge-only support by +0.024 [+0.018,+0.029] and the mean of ten exact-degree rewires by +0.011 [+0.005,+0.017]. The native-panel effect declined from +0.016 at 200 genes to +0.009 at 1000 genes; the 1000-200 interaction was -0.006 [-0.011,-0.002]. The primary graph-support comparison was formulated and conducted during peer-review revision rather than planned as an a priori confirmatory study. All three external models passed implementation-specific checks. Across 36 protocol-matched dataset-scale contrasts, 32 were within the descriptive ±0.030 reference envelope and four were outside, all favouring the external model. These results demonstrate a modest empirical predictive improvement under the evaluated matched protocol; they do not by themselves establish practical biological relevance.

records.title: AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing: from genome mining to the artificial intelligence virtual cell.
records.abstract: Fungi are important chassis organisms for sustainable biomanufacturing owing to their strong secretion capacity, metabolic diversity, and adaptability to industrial processes. Driven by the rapid development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), computational approaches that enable machines to learn patterns from data and make predictions, together with omics technologies and synthetic biology, data- and model-driven strategies are increasingly reshaping fungal cell factory design and optimization. This review summarizes recent advances in AI-enabled fungal biomanufacturing, covering AI-assisted genome mining, enzyme and pathway analysis, genome editing, metabolic network modeling, and intelligent fermentation control. The review further highlights the emerging concept of the artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC), which integrates multi-omics data, mechanistic modeling, and machine learning-based approaches into a unified multiscale framework for simulating dynamic cellular behaviors. The technical foundations and potential applications of AIVC in fungal metabolic engineering, drug discovery, agriculture, and environmental biotechnology are reviewed. Finally, key challenges-data quality and standardization, cross-scale model integration and interpretability, and the gap between in silico prediction and experimental validation-are highlighted. This review provides a systematic perspective on the role of AI and virtual cell technologies in advancing next generation fungal biotechnology.

records.title: PHAROS: turning single-cell perturbation models into target-directed drug-combination screens.
records.abstract: Combination therapies are central to cancer treatment, but exhaustive screening is impractical. We introduce PHAROS, a framework that turns a pretrained single-cell perturbation model into a target-directed search engine for drug combinations. PHAROS predicts how a cell population changes under a drug, one drug at a time, then chains these predictions together to simulate drug combinations. It scores each simulated outcome against the desired target state and uses a search algorithm to find the most promising combinations, all without retraining the underlying model. Across two independent combinatorial perturbation datasets, PHAROS recovered exact or mechanism-matched two-drug responses in cell lines, both seen and unseen during model training. Its rankings were specific to the requested conversion and were not explained by single-drug effects, additive effects, or shared mechanism of action. In exploratory analyses of patient-derived metastatic HR+/HER2- breast tumors and basal cell carcinoma (BCC), PHAROS prioritized FDA-approved regimens, distinguished combinations by their predicted tumor-versus-immune objective profiles, and nominated pathway-level hypotheses, while explicitly identifying both tumor cohorts as outside the model's supported distribution. PHAROS provides a modular route from pretrained virtual-cell models to inverse, single-cell combination-screening platforms.

records.title: Programming biological behavior with AI-guided de novo protein design.
records.abstract: Driven by advances in artificial intelligence, de novo protein design can now generate diverse molecular functions from the ground up, achieving remarkable success in engineering binders against many macromolecular targets. Here, we provide a perspective on how de novo design can progress beyond bimolecular interactions toward the bottom-up construction of protein reaction networks. We highlight how programmable, modular, and controllable de novo components can drive complex, emergent biological behaviors. Overcoming current challenges-including designable protein dynamics, multi-step functionalities, and non-equilibrium systems-is essential for this transition. With continued foundational method improvements, the field is poised to pioneer precise protein perturbations for systems-level insight and to engineer emergent cellular behaviors like signal amplification, decision-making, and error correction de novo to fundamentally advance synthetic biology, biotechnology, and medicine.

records.title: Multi-Objective Molecular Generation via Actor-Critic Regulated by Adaptive Cooperative Evolution.
records.abstract: Many complex diseases involve intricate and interdependent biological mechanisms, making multi-target drug design therapeutically important. However, existing molecular generation models often struggle to balance conflicting property requirements, maintain structural exploration, and avoid premature convergence during reinforcement learning. To address these challenges, we propose CMIR-RL, a reinforcement learning-based molecular generation model that integrates cooperative crossover-mutation exploration, structure-based intrinsic rewards, and Pareto-based multi-objective optimization. In CMIR-RL, mutation and crossover networks synergistically guide the agent to balance exploration and exploitation, while Pareto-front-guided reward assignment updates the generation policy under multiple property constraints. Experiments on a three-objective polypharmacology task show that CMIR-RL significantly improves desirability from 0.8868 to 0.9542 over the baseline method, while maintaining competitive validity, uniqueness, and diversity. Additional GuacaMol results further indicate competitive generalization across goal-directed molecular generation tasks. These results show that CMIR-RL is an effective reinforcement learning strategy for early-stage multi-objective molecular design.

records.title: Virus-like particle vaccines: from antigen architecture to antigen presentation and adaptive immune responses.
records.abstract: Virus-like particles (VLPs) mimic key structural features of native viruses while lacking a replication-competent viral genome, combining favorable safety with multivalent antigen presentation and strong immunogenicity. Yet, how VLP design influences the quality and persistence of adaptive immunity remains incompletely understood. This review examines relevant literature identified through targeted searches on recent advances in VLP engineering, with emphasis on particle architecture, antigen-display strategies, and structural determinants of immune recognition. We discuss how VLPs facilitate antigen presentation by antigen-presenting cells and shape CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses, immune memory, and T follicular helper cell-B-cell interactions within germinal centers. Emerging approaches linking VLP design with humoral and cellular immunity are also considered. The next generation of VLP vaccines will require a transition from empirical enhancement of immunogenicity toward precision engineering of immune responses. A major challenge is to establish robust and transferable structure-immunity relationships while addressing manufacturing feasibility, quality control, potency assessment, and product comparability. Advances in computational protein design, structural biology, and high-dimensional immune profiling are expected to enable increasingly quantitative and mechanism-based optimization of VLP platforms. However, fully predictive control over human immune responses will remain a complex challenge.

records.title: MolecureAI: an agentic AI platform for autonomous drug discovery.
records.abstract: Accelerating the identification of viable drug candidates across therapeutic areas demands autonomous systems for molecular generation that enforce chemical correctness by structural invariants rather than model capability. We present MolecureAI, an autonomous AI agent architecture for closed-loop drug discovery with cost-ordered cascade evaluation that addresses four capability gaps unresolved across the field: autonomous design strategy selection, persistent cross-campaign structural memory, in-loop ADMET safety gating, and literature-scale evidence integration into the generative loop. A cost-ordered cascade concentrates full structure-based evaluation on a small pre-filtered survivor set, achieving a 2.5 × reduction in candidates advanced relative to those generated. An in-loop metabolic gate enforces Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity (ADMET) safety by writing flagged reactive substructures to a per-target learned state, suppressing identified liabilities from all subsequent generation rounds. A persistent campaign memory influences generation trajectories by embedding prior structural success and failure patterns directly into the design context. We validate these architectural invariants across three structurally diverse benchmark targets (EGFR, KRAS G 12 C , and BRD4) through a five-condition component ablation and a controlled memory ablation, and confirm generator agnosticism across four language-model backends via a deterministic recalibration layer that overrides backend self-evaluation bias. Without explicit chemotype instruction, the pipeline computationally converged toward candidates bearing the 4-anilinoquinazoline scaffold characteristic of the approved inhibitors erlotinib and gefitinib, from structural feedback alone. Persistent campaign memory showed directional but non-significant trends toward lower inter-round score variance and higher late-stage advance rate ( n ≈ 90 per condition; all p > 0.20 ). The component ablation reveals that optimizing for a single objective collapses performance on others; only full orchestration resolves this tension. Advancement rates above 79% across all backends confirm that the validated properties are generator-agnostic, enforced by architectural invariants rather than model capability. All reported outcomes are properties of the computational generation process; prospective biochemical validation of the advanced candidates remains the primary direction for future work.

records.title: Functional alignment of protein language models via reinforcement learning.
records.abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) enable generative design of novel protein sequences but remain fundamentally misaligned with protein engineering goals, as they lack explicit understanding of function and often fail to improve properties beyond those found in nature. We introduce Reinforcement Learning from eXperimental Feedback (RLXF), a general framework that aligns protein language models with experimentally measured functional objectives, drawing inspiration from the methods used to align large language models like ChatGPT. Applied across five diverse protein families, RLXF improves generation of high-functioning variants beyond pre-trained baselines. We demonstrate this with CreiLOV, an oxygen-independent fluorescent protein, where RLXF-aligned models generate sequences with significantly enhanced fluorescence, including the most fluorescent CreiLOV variants reported to date. Our results indicate that RLXF-aligned models effectively integrate the evolutionary knowledge encoded in pre-trained pLMs with experimental observations, improving the success rate of generated sequences and enabling the discovery of synergistic mutation combinations that are difficult to identify through zero-shot or evolutionary approaches. RLXF provides a scalable and accessible approach to steer generative models toward desired biochemical properties, enabling function-driven protein design beyond the limits of natural evolution.

records.title: Perspectives on tissue-selective insulin derivatives.
records.abstract: Insulin is a central regulator of metabolic homoeostasis with diverse, tissue-specific actions across multiple organs. Despite major advances in insulin formulations, current therapies rely on systemic delivery and do not reproduce the physiological distribution of endogenous insulin, resulting in non-physiological tissue exposure and associated metabolic limitations. In this perspective, we discuss emerging strategies aimed at achieving tissue-selective insulin action, including molecular engineering of insulin analogues, modulation of insulin receptor isoform specificity and targeted delivery approaches. Attention is given to hepato-preferential, muscle-directed, brain-targeted and adipose-modulating strategies, highlighting their mechanistic basis, therapeutic potential and inherent limitations. While proof of principle has been established for several approaches, challenges remain in balancing tissue selectivity with whole-body metabolic control. Advances in protein design and delivery technologies may ultimately enable the development of next-generation insulin therapies that better mimic physiological insulin action and improve clinical outcomes in metabolic and neurodegenerative diseases.

records.title: The $100 genome: three platforms reshaping clinical genomics.
records.abstract: In 2026, three high-throughput sequencing platforms approached the widely publicised sub-$100 30× human genome. Behind these figures, which reflect consumable prices rather than total cost of ownership, the more consequential shift is the end of single-vendor dominance: these systems make comprehensive genomic profiling and multi-omic liquid biopsy feasible in small batches.

records.title: Emerging precision diagnostics in genitourinary cancers.
records.abstract: Genitourinary tumors comprise distinct entities with different epidemiological background, molecular alterations and clinical outcomes, underlining the need for precision diagnostics. Recent advances in molecular technologies have facilitated the increasing use of molecular testing in routine diagnostics. These tests have important roles in diagnosis, risk stratification, and therapeutic tailoring, and are both tissue-based and liquid biopsy-based. Examples include 1) high-end (epi)genomic arrays, such as mRNA-based arrays for prostate cancer; 2) noninvasive circulating biomarkers (DNA mutations or DNA methylation) in bladder cancer, and serum/plasma microRNA (micrcoRNA-371a-3p) testing in testicular germ cell tumors; 3) as well as targeted assays focused on immunohistochemistry and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) for renal and penile cancers. In this review we cover the application of these tests in routine practice at a molecular pathology lab. These tests are at different stages of development and establishment in routine practice. As molecular testing increases, so does the relevance of pre-analytics, sample selection and morphological assessment, which are key for achieving reliable results. Integration of molecular tests is set to contribute to precision medicine in genitourinary cancers, contributing to better selection of patients for targeted therapies. Centralization of techniques, human resources and resources is critical to establish effective molecular testing frameworks for the community.

records.title: Serum extracellular vesicle-associated SNORD54 adds diagnostic information to CEA and CYFRA21-1 in non-small cell lung cancer: a case-control development study.
records.abstract: Blood-based biomarkers that complement established serum markers may improve molecular classification of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). We evaluated whether SNORD54 and SNORD41 measured in a serum extracellular vesicle (EV)-enriched fraction provided incremental discrimination beyond carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and cytokeratin 19 fragment 21-1 (CYFRA21-1). This single-center case-control biomarker-development study included serum samples from patients with histologically or cytologically confirmed NSCLC and contemporaneous healthy controls. Supporting expression evidence was assessed in paired lung adenocarcinoma and lung squamous cell carcinoma datasets and in 48 paired formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded NSCLC specimens. Serum analyses included gene-specific cohorts and a common complete-case cohort with SNORD54, SNORD41, CEA, and CYFRA21-1 measurements. Logistic regression models were compared using paired DeLong tests. Model parsimony, adjustment for age, sex, and smoking, locked Stage I-II and Stage I subgroup analyses, U6-normalization sensitivity analyses, and 2,000-resample bootstrap internal validation were performed. The complete-case cohort comprised 98 patients with NSCLC and 79 healthy controls. Adding SNORD54 to CEA and CYFRA21-1 increased the AUC from 0.851(95% confidence interval [CI], 0.795-0.907) to 0.951 (95% CI, 0.920-0.982; ΔAUC, 0.100; 95% CI, 0.050-0.150; P<0.001). At the development-derived cutoff, the three-marker model achieved 85.7% sensitivity and 94.9% specificity. SNORD41 did not improve the SNORD54-containing model (ΔAUC, 0.0003; P=0.480; likelihood-ratio P=0.953) and increased both Akaike and Bayesian information criteria. With coefficients and the cutoff fixed from the overall cohort, the three-marker model achieved AUCs of 0.904 (95% CI, 0.843-0.964) for Stage I-II disease and 0.882 (95% CI, 0.804-0.960) for Stage I disease. SNORD54 remained informative after adjustment for age, sex, and smoking. The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.948. U6 Ct values differed between diagnostic groups; associations of both snoRNAs with case status persisted in sensitivity models accounting for U6 Ct. SNORD54 measured in a serum EV-enriched fraction provided incremental discrimination beyond CEA and CYFRA21-1 in this NSCLC case-control cohort. The parsimonious SNORD54 + CEA + CYFRA21-1 model retained discrimination in locked early-stage subgroup analyses and showed limited apparent optimism after bootstrap correction. Independent validation in cohorts that include benign pulmonary nodules and other relevant lung diseases, together with standardized EV processing and validated RNA normalization, will define the clinical transportability of this three-marker panel.

records.title: Assessing the impact of parental linear gene normalization on the performance of statistical models for circular RNA differential expression analysis.
records.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have emerged as promising non-invasive cancer biomarkers due to their stability, abundance in body fluids, and regulatory potential. However, circRNA differential expression analysis (DEA) remains challenging, owing to a lack of consensus on important preprocessing strategies such as filtering and normalization. While well-established bulk RNA-sequencing frameworks are commonly applied to circRNA data, newer approaches such as CIRI-DE (part of CIRI3 suite) integrate linear and circular transcript information to improve detection. Despite developments, an assessment of these integrative strategies is lacking, and the critical impact of filtering on DEA model performance has not been comprehensively evaluated. In this study, we evaluated the impact of multiple normalization and filtering strategies on circRNA DEA using experimental datasets, including two in-house blood platelet sets and semi-parametric simulated in silico datasets. Our results emphasize the importance of selecting an appropriate filtering threshold, as overly lenient filtering can reduce model performance across datasets. We found edgeR's filterByExpr() strategy particularly effective in handling zero counts in circRNA data, while also generating the most reliable results across most datasets.Furthermore, by incorporating linear and circular information as described in CIRI-DE, most methods identified a higher number of DE circRNAs compared to circular counts alone. Notably, circRNAs identified by both CIRI-DE and the modified bulk RNA-sequencing pipelines showed substantial overlap. Our findings demonstrate that automated filtering combined with linear-aware normalization significantly enhances the sensitivity and reproducibility of circRNA DEA, providing a standardized framework for more reliable biomarker discovery in transcriptomic research.

records.title: Cell-free DNA methylation markers in the diagnosis of hepatitis B virus-related- hepatocellular carcinoma: a review.
records.abstract: Hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, and its prognosis largely depends on detection at an early, potentially curable stage. However, current surveillance strategies based on ultrasonography and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) have limited sensitivity, highlighting the need for more accurate and non-invasive biomarkers. This review examines the emerging role of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation analysis as a liquid biopsy approach for the early detection and surveillance of HBV-HCC. Aberrant DNA methylation is a major epigenetic event in hepatocarcinogenesis, contributing to the silencing of tumor suppressor genes, while the HBV X protein can further promote methylation dysregulation through its interactions with DNA methyltransferases. Clinically, specific cfDNA methylation markers and multi-feature panels have demonstrated promising diagnostic performance for HCC detection. More complex multi-feature cfDNA models integrating methylation with additional fragmentomic features have achieved up to 95.42% sensitivity and 97.67% specificity (AUC = 0.997) for differentiating HCC from liver cirrhosis, while maintaining a high sensitivity of 90.0% for early-stage HCC detection. In specific cohorts, methylation-based approaches have complemented AFP, detecting nearly 75% of early malignancies missed by AFP alone and increasing the AUC of combined predictive model from 0.87 to 0.90. Furthermore, combined mutation-methylation assays that concurrently profile genetic mutations and hypermethylation patterns have achieved validation AUC values as high as 0.93. Overall, cfDNA methylation-based approaches exhibit promising diagnostic performance compared with conventional biomarkers in specific cohorts. However, prospective validation and direct head-to-head comparisons with existing surveillance strategies are still required before their clinical utility can be established.

records.title: Molecular biomarkers for diagnosis, prognosis, precision therapy, and immunotherapy in cholangiocarcinoma, cHCC-CCA, and HCC.
records.abstract: Primary liver cancers include hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma (cHCC-CCA), and rarer hepatic malignancies. Their biomarker landscapes differ substantially. HCC has many approved systemic therapies, yet most are still selected through clinical context, liver function, tumor burden, and treatment line. By contrast, iCCA and broader biliary tract cancers (BTCs) have fewer patients but multiple treatment-directing genomic alterations, including FGFR2 fusions or rearrangements, IDH1 mutations, HER2 positivity, BRAF V600E, NTRK or RET fusions, and microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) or deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) status. cHCC-CCA adds a diagnostic layer because lineage classification and sampling adequacy influence whether HCC-based or BTC-based evidence is more relevant. This review organizes biomarkers by the treatment decision they are expected to support. It covers curative intent and locoregional risk stratification, molecularly guided systemic therapy, immune-state assessment, dynamic monitoring, resistance reassessment, and translational readiness. Across these settings, biomarker value depends on clinical action, evidence maturity, assay feasibility, and timing. The review separates decision-ready markers, trial-enrichment tools, monitoring assays, and mechanistic signatures.
